title: Brutus is an honourable man.
html_source: Repeated line in Mark Antony’s speech from III.ii of Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar. In the play Antony’s speech parodies Brutus’s preceding speech to demonstrate the dishonorable nature of Brutus and co.’s murder of Julius Caesar; the repeated use of the phrase “Brutus is an honourable man” is highly sarcastic. The purpose of the reference here is similarly sarcastic, mocking the pliability of “reserved” women’s innocence.
